Extending to approximately 27.5 hectares (68 acres), this exceptional and historically significant holding at Killineer offers a rare opportunity to acquire prime agricultural land in a highly accessible location just 4km from Drogheda town centre and 2.6km from the M1 Retail Park. Situated within the Dublin commuter belt, the lands combine productive farmland with excellent connectivity and long-term strategic appeal. Given its location on the outskirts of a growing urban centre, the property may also offer future potential for alternative uses, subject to obtaining the necessary planning permissions and any required rezoning.

LANDS AT KILLINEER
The lands are of very good quality, well maintained and currently in excellent heart. The fertile soils are ideally suited to both tillage and grassland enterprises, providing versatility for a wide range of agricultural uses. The holding is laid out in practical, well-defined divisions with excellent road frontage and three access points, ensuring efficient day-to-day management and ease of operation. There is also freshwater stream going through the lands. Productive land of this calibre, in such strong condition, is becoming increasingly difficult to source in this highly regarded farming district. There is approximately 550 metres of road frontage onto the R132 national road.
Occupying an enviable position at Killineer, one of the most desirable rural locations in the Drogheda hinterland, the property combines the benefits of a peaceful countryside setting with exceptional accessibility. Situated approximately 4km from Drogheda town centre and just 2.6km from the M1 Retail Park, the lands enjoy easy access to one of Ireland's most important economic corridors, strategically positioned between Dublin and Belfast. The M1 Motorway, Dublin Airport, Drogheda Port and the town's extensive rail and transport infrastructure are all within easy reach, underpinning the ongoing appeal of the area for both agricultural and investment purchasers.
Drogheda has evolved into one of Ireland's most significant regional growth centres, benefiting from substantial population growth, increasing employment opportunities and continued investment in infrastructure and services. As the largest town in Ireland and a key commercial hub on the Dublin Belfast corridor, its strategic importance continues to strengthen, supported by the presence of Drogheda Port, expanding business activity and strong commuter connections to the capital.
In addition to its obvious agricultural merits, the property's strategic location on the outskirts of Drogheda may present future opportunities for alternative uses, subject to obtaining all necessary planning permissions and any required rezoning. As urban centres continue to expand and the demand for residential, commercial and employment land evolves, holdings of this scale, accessibility and profile are becoming increasingly scarce. While currently presented as a productive agricultural holding, its location within a well-established growth corridor further enhances its long-term strategic appeal as an investment asset.

Whether acquired as a working farm, an investment holding or as an addition to an existing agricultural enterprise, this property represents a rare opportunity to secure a substantial block of prime County Louth land in a location of proven demand and enduring appeal. Opportunities to acquire land of this quality and scale in the Killineer area seldom come to the market.

A PLACE IN IRISH HISTORY
Few properties can claim a place in the story of modern Ireland. On 29th September 1979, these lands at Killineer became the setting for one of the most significant events ever held in Ireland when Pope John Paul II, now Saint John Paul II, visited as part of the first Papal pilgrimage to Ireland. Chosen for its elevated natural amphitheatre, accessibility and proximity to Drogheda, the site welcomed an estimated 300,000 people who gathered to witness a historic address by the Pontiff. It was here that Pope John Paul II delivered his famous appeal for peace, a message that resonated far beyond Ireland and remains one of the defining moments of his visit. Following the ceremony, the Pope travelled through the assembled crowds in the Popemobile, creating memories that remain vivid for those fortunate enough to be present. Today, a commemorative stone marks the exact location from which Saint John Paul II addressed the nation, providing a lasting reminder of this extraordinary chapter in the history of the land.
Rarely does an opportunity arise to acquire property associated with an event of such national and international significance. These lands occupy a unique place in Ireland's cultural, religious and historical heritage.
